title: ChatGPT's paraffin-oil advice may have saved Islam Adel's 17-year-old cousin after an aluminum phosphide “grain pill” ingestion in Assiut
summary: A Facebook post of 24 May 2025 credits ChatGPT with first aid. Assiut Faculty of Medicine dean Alaa Attia says that the youth had no phosphine symptoms and said he threw the pill into water.
account: El Balad (24 May 2025, 12:39) reproduces a Facebook post by Islam Adel, a commercial-control inspector. He wrote it at 1 a.m. after “24 hours” had passed since his cousin Mohamed Yousry (17) swallowed part of a “grain pill” (aluminum phosphide). The pill came from samples Adel had seized and kept at the family's old house. The cousin took it after a quarrel with his father. Adel writes that the Abnoub central hospital refused the case. He writes that within minutes he asked ChatGPT for the best course. It advised paraffin oil to coat the pill and limit phosphine release. The youth drank a bottle from a pharmacy before they went to Assiut University Hospital's poison reception. Doctors there said there was no treatment protocol and the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The cousin stayed conscious, vomited for hours and was discharged stable. Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post and the reply of Dr Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said precise medical examinations showed no signs or symptoms of swallowing the pill. The youth denied taking it and admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental and not officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him and he categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds toxicologist Dr Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says oils are indeed a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Cairo University toxicologist Dr Nermin Hamdi that Assiut University denied the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil is first aid, not treatment. The Monitor lists 13 syndications. Al Arabiya's syndication was not available. The ingestion date is not fixed by any source.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant. The cousin used it for emergency first-aid advice and, by his account, for instructions during hospital care. The claimed benefit (a survival) is outside any stated purpose of the system.
system: ChatGPT (OpenAI), described in the post as 'an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5'
model_version: GPT-5 trial version, per the cousin's post; unverified
deployer: Islam Adel, the patient's cousin, as a consumer user
location: Abnoub and Assiut University Hospital, Assiut Governorate, Egypt
segment: Consumer chatbot used for first-aid advice

ratings.reason: The survival claim rests on the cousin's post. The dean says that there was no poisoning to survive. No outcome attributable to the advice is therefore documented.
Al Jazeera Mubasher and Dostor report experts warning that the “trend” could kill. No wider effect is documented.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT's output (advice to give paraffin oil, then nine bottles in turn with breathing exercises) is documented only by the cousin's own post. The chat transcripts were not published (“too many to publish all”, per Masrawy's summary of the post). Dean Alaa Attia contradicts its effect: he says that the patient had no clinical signs of phosphine poisoning and denied swallowing the pill. Dr Nermin Hamdi's report that Assiut University denied the case involved the grain pill also contradicts it. Dr Mahmoud Amr says that oil is a recognized first aid but not a cure. Whether the hospital followed any of the AI's instructions is unsupported by any source other than the post.

headline: ChatGPT's first-aid advice may have saved a teen in Assiut

later.note: The next day the dean of Assiut University's Faculty of Medicine told Masrawy that the youth showed no clinical signs of phosphine poisoning and had categorically denied swallowing the pill, and on 26 May a toxicologist told Al Jazeera Mubasher that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case has no scientific basis.
later.quote: فى المقابل، أوضح عميد كلية طب أسيوط، لـ"مصراوي" أن الشاب، البالغ من العمر نحو 17 عامًا، لم تظهر عليه أي أعراض سريرية تشير إلى تعرضه لتسمم بمادة الفوسفين الناتجة عن قرص الغلة، وهي أعراض معروفة وواضحة في مثل هذه الحالات. وأضاف أن الفريق الطبي تابع الحالة بدقة، ووجّه للشاب عدة استفسارات حول تناوله للقرص، إلا أنه نفى ذلك بشكل قاطع، مؤكدًا أنه ألقى القرص في حوض ماء ولم يبتلعه.
